releaseName: Start your career record from a conversation
summary: A person with no CV can start their career record from a conversation: while the record has no document, the Career evidence card and Home offer Tell it in a conversation beside Add documents, the interviewer offers four starting topics (work history, education, skills, something to be proud of), and the first confirmed summary becomes the record's first evidence (#2732, #2733, #2734). Signed-in users now see the written career interview (#2735). The Career evidence card is simpler, and technical choices across the app sit under one Advanced options fold (#2736, #2739, #2740, #2741). A paid application's credit now covers its Prepare calls under a fair-use limit of 20 drafts, guides and research runs (#2680). Above the workspace cost cap, a run picks evidence by job requirement (#2667). Credit packs can be bought on a Buy credits screen where the operator has set up Stripe, and a paid checkout grants its credits (#2708, #2709, #2711, #2712). The interview guide writer has room for its answer, its research runs every planned query within its cap, and failed calls count in the cost (#2718, #2719). A cover letter says when it names no employer or dates because the record holds none (#2725). Each candidate record has a plain name, and the record area is one compact bar (#2730, #2742). A large source stays in a career profile update whatever the number of sources (#2729).
knownLimitations: Starting from a conversation needs the server's interviewer model; without it the panel says so after Start. Signed-in users get the written interview only: live voice shows with the owner token, and a Free plan's conversation counts against its 20 model calls a day until the plan rule is built (#2750). Agents cannot add text evidence yet (#2751). Buying a credit pack needs Stripe set up by the operator, which staging does not have; refunds are not built (#2710), self-service sign-up is not built, and whether prices include VAT is open (#2677). The interview guide's paid walk is partial (#2623). Holding back a fact withholds the whole source passage it was quoted from. The dating of relative source ages is not yet checked against a live search (#2579). On the hosted staging service, drafting needs model screening, which stays off there until Claude on Vertex AI is available. Assistant sign-in needs an identity provider, which staging does not have yet. French is beta until the French quality gate (milestone 83) runs. The Steps section appears only for runs the server executed since traces were recorded.
